data.title: EQT Healthcare Growth to acquire majority stake in specialty European pharmaceutical business, Kelso Pharma
data.description:
• Kelso Pharma is a fast-growing specialty pharmaceutical group with a portfolio of approximately 14 medicines, mainly for endocrine, gastrointestinal and central nervous system conditions
  • The company has built a commercial platform in the UK, with a growing presence across Europe and an expanding portfolio of medicines for niche patient populations
  • EQT will support Kelso Pharma's expansion across Europe through investment in its commercial capabilities, new product launches and selective acquisitions and licensing agreements

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EQT is pleased to announce that EQT Healthcare Growth ("EQT") has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a majority stake in Kelso Pharma ("Kelso", or the "Company"), from healthcare investment firm Apposite Capital. Kelso's management team, led by Chief Executive Officer, Dr Tom Stratford, will continue to lead the Company.

Kelso Pharma is a European specialty pharmaceutical group focused on medicines for niche patient populations, which are sold through its own UK-based commercial infrastructure, and exported to more than 30 countries globally. Founded in 2021 with the support of Apposite Capital, Kelso has expanded both through strong organic growth of in-market drugs as well as value-accretive M&A - through the acquisition of Stirling Anglian Pharmaceuticals, Velit Biopharma (now Kelso Pharma Italy) and ALTURiX - and in-licensing deals. Kelso Pharma has approximately 14 medicines in its portfolio, mainly for endocrine, gastrointestinal and central nervous system conditions, and is expanding its product range to provide additional medicines addressing patients' unmet needs.

EQT Healthcare Growth seeks to scale healthcare companies by strengthening their commercial capabilities and expanding their reach, drawing on EQT's 30-year track record in the healthcare sector and its global footprint to help companies grow internationally. EQT brings its healthcare expertise and international network to support the Company to broaden its product portfolio, expand into new European markets, pursue selective acquisitions and in-licensing and build on its specialty pharmaceutical offering.

Dr Mark Braganza, Partner at EQT Healthcare Growth, said: "Healthcare systems across Europe are increasingly looking to specialist companies to serve patient groups that larger pharmaceutical businesses often overlook. With an experienced team, its own commercial infrastructure and a portfolio serving niche patient populations, Kelso has built a strong UK-based business with the foundations to grow as a pan-European platform. We look forward to bringing EQT's deep healthcare experience and global network to support Tom and his team as they scale Kelso across Europe."

Dr Tom Stratford, Chief Executive Officer of Kelso Pharma, said: "We founded Kelso Pharma to bring specialist medicines to patients with conditions that are often underserved and to the healthcare systems that treat them. Since then, we have established a strong position in the UK and begun to extend our reach into Europe. We are proud to partner with EQT, whose deep, global sector experience will help us develop Kelso Pharma into a leading pan-European specialty pharmaceutical company. This builds on the support we have received from Apposite since 2021 and is testament to the work of the whole Kelso team."

Sam Gray, Managing Partner at Apposite Capital, said: "Kelso Pharma is a textbook example of the growth that Apposite seeks to unlock through its specialist approach to investing in private health and life sciences businesses. Under Tom's leadership, Kelso has combined organic and acquisitive growth, including bringing new value-added medicines to market. EQT's investment provides not just significant additional capital but also an endorsement of the Kelso team's strategic vision."

The transaction is subject to customary conditions and approvals. It is expected to close during Q1 2027.

ContactEQT Press Office, press@eqtpartners.com

data.title: China Water Affairs Announces FY2026/27 Interim Results, Resilient Core Water Supply Business, Continuously Improved Balance Sheet
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 27, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - China Water Affairs Group Limited ('China Water Affairs' or the 'Company', stock code: 0855.HK), a leading integrated water operator in China, today announced the interim results of the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively known as the 'Group') for the 6 months ended 30 September 2026 ('the Reporting Period').

Amid a complex and ever-changing external environment and macroeconomic challenges, the Group has resolutely advanced its high-quality development strategy, continuing to allocate resources to its core businesses and cash-flow-generating operations. As strict controls on capital expenditures and debt refinancing measures continue to be implemented, the Group's debt levels have trended downward in a healthy manner, while financing costs have steadily declined, leading to positive improvements in the balance sheet. The core water supply business has maintained steady growth driven by inelastic demand and the implementation of tariff hikes, while technology-driven improvements in operational efficiency have further contributed to the Group's positive performance.

During the Reporting Period, the Group recorded a total revenue of approximately HK$5.032 billion, representing a year-on-year decrease of 2.9%. Gross profit was approximately HK$1.73billion, down 5.3% year-on-year. Net profit amounted to approximately HK$982 million, a year-on-year increase of 2.7%, while profit attributable to shareholders was approximately HK$665 million, representing an increase of 16.4%. To reward shareholders for their support, the Board of Directors announced an interim dividend of 10 Hong Kong cents per share, representing a 23.1% decrease compared to the same period last year.

Reviewing the Reporting Period, the Group's core water supply business delivered outstanding performance, with both revenue and profit increasing. Although revenue from urban water supply construction services, installation and maintenance services decreased by 16.5% and 3.9% year-over-year respectively, driven by steady growth in water sales volume and tariff hikes, core urban water supply operating revenue rose 7.8% year-over-year to approximately HK$1.943 billion. This propelled the urban water supply segment's revenue and profit to record robust growth of 3.1% and 7.5% respectively, reaching approximately HK$3.373 billion and HK$1.012 billion. The direct drinking water segment saw a significant improvement in profitability following strategic restructuring and a focus on developing high-quality projects within designated water supply areas. During the period, segment revenue grew steadily by 0.7% to approximately HK$265 million, while segment profit surged 20.9% year-over-year to approximately HK$90.1 million, with the profit margin widening to 34.0%. Meanwhile, the Group implemented cost-cutting and efficiency-enhancing measures through AI-powered smart water management and organizational optimization. During the Reporting Period, the total number of employees decreased by 6.8% year-over-year to approximately 9,600, while sales and administrative expenses were reduced by 2.5% year-over-year, and the leakage rate fell by 0.5 percentage points year-over-year to 13.8%. During the Reporting Period, the environmental protection segment was affected by factors such as the reduction in the scale of construction projects and a decrease in the scope of the ExxonMobil project due to external oil price fluctuation. As a result, segment revenue and profit declined year-over-year by 21.3% and 27.5% respectively to approximately HK$655 million and HK$266 million. Overall, the urban water supply and direct-drinking water businesses further increased their share of the Group's total revenue to 72.3%, continuing to serve as a core pillar of the business.

During the Reporting Period, the Group's strict control over capital expenditures has yielded significant results. The Group's direct capital expenditures related to water infrastructure construction fell to the HK$1 billion level, driving a further 0.5 percentage point reduction in the asset-to-liability ratio to 63.7%. The Group actively extended debt maturities and broadened financing channels, successfully repaying a US$350 million bond this May, which increased the proportion of long-term debt to total borrowings to 75.6% and resulted in a more robust debt structure. The Group also continued to deepen its cooperation with financial institutions and effectively reduced cash payment costs through cross-currency swap arrangements and the refinancing of existing project loans, keeping total borrowing costs on a downward trend during the period, even as external U.S. interest rates remained in a rate-hiking cycle.

The Group continues to advance its light-asset strategy. As of September 30, its outsourced operations spanned more than 20 regions, with total water sales volume reaching nearly 60 million metric tons, accounting for 7.8% of total water sales volume. Recently, the Group has been actively and comprehensively expanding such projects to gradually achieve a balanced approach combining light and heavy assets, while leveraging synergies to generate higher marginal returns.

As digital and intelligent technologies were gradually implemented across various water supply units, processes such as pipeline operations, energy consumption monitoring, and leak detection were further optimized during the Reporting Period. The Group has now integrated AI tools into its daily operational processes, enabling real-time monitoring of operational parameters and rapid response to abnormal conditions. Digital and intelligent technologies, exemplified by AI tools, have become a key technical pillar in the Group's cost-reduction and efficiency-enhancement initiatives, driving continuous improvement in the water supply segment's operational metrics. In particular, the leakage rate has been further reduced to an average of 13.8%.

Looking forward, 2027 marks a critical window of opportunity for the in-depth implementation of the 15th Five-Year Plan. With the country allocating special funds to support the renovation of pipelines and aging residential communities, coupled with the accelerated transfer of secondary water supply operations and the implementation of tariff hikes mechanisms, the industry is benefiting from a dual boost of funding and pricing. The Group will resolutely advance the high-quality development strategy, enforce stringent controls over capital expenditure, leverage AI-powered smart water management to drive the transformation of its growth model toward efficiency and value, and achieve 'cost reduction, efficiency improvement, and leak control' through digital management, thereby enhancing earnings per metric ton of water and free cash flow. Meanwhile, the Group will continue to adhere to the principles of financial soundness and cash flow priority, reduce debt and financing costs, implement ESG governance, and uphold the philosophy of 'Water oriented and kindness to society', creating sustainable long-term value for shareholders and society through solid performance.

About China Water Affairs Group Limited

China Water Affairs Group Limited is a leading professional, international, market-oriented and cross-regional water services operator in China and the only Hong Kong listed company focusing on-tap water business. Headquartered in Hong Kong, it has operations management centers in Beijing and Shenzhen. The Group (including associate companies) mainly engages in urban water supply, pipeline direct drinking water, sewage treatment and drainage and other related value-added services in Chinese Mainland. Its services cover more than 30 million people across 24 provinces, direct-administered municipalities and autonomous regions. The Group has established a leading position as a full-service operator in China's water affairs market. Its management comprises of veteran experts in the water industry with an insight into government policies and services management. The Company's shares were included in the first batch of securities eligible for trading through Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect in 2016 and have been the constituent stock in the FTSE Environmental Opportunities Asia Pacific Index since 2009.

This press release is issued by Ever Bloom (HK) Communications Consultants Group Limited on behalf of China Water Affairs Group Limited.

data.title: Honda Motor October Production Declines
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (7267.T), the Japanese auto major, Friday reported lower worldwide automobile production for October compared to the same period last year.

However, October sales in Japan and exports increased year over year.

October automobile production worldwide decreased for the ninth consecutive month to 298,619 units from 302,671 units last year.

The company said that the October Japanese production has declined for the third consecutive month to 60,138 units from 63,662 units previous year.

Outside of Japan, October production reduced for the tenth consecutive month to 238,481 units from 239,009 units prior year.

Nonetheless, total October sales in Japan increased to 51,336 units from 48,955 units a year ago.

Total October exports rose to 14,258 units from 9357 units same period last year.

Today, shares closed at ¥1776, up 0.51% on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

data.title: Chinese Shares Lifted as Beijing Signals More Market Support
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Chinese stocks were lifted as authorities reiterated support for capital markets and vowed stabilization policies, amid increased volatility in global markets.

According to state media Xinhua News Agency, Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting focused on market reforms.

The meeting noted that "the capital market is crucial to the overall economic development," and China would improve its market stabilization mechanism and introduce new policies to promote stable and healthy markets, Xinhua reported.

As part of this, the role of China's state investors--the so-called "national team"--in stabilizing the markets and countering volatility would be strengthened. Also, efforts would be made to optimize the function of Central Huijin, a unit of state-owned sovereign wealth fund China Investment, as a quasi-stabilization fund.

It also said that Beijing will guide medium- and long-term funds into the markets and listed companies should be encouraged to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases.

Although the measures look to be mostly reiterating previously announced ones, the language has shifted incrementally to show a bit more urgency and tangible action, according to ING chief China economist Lynn Song.

Chinese stock markets have weakened in recent months, broadly in line with global market as investors cool on tech-related companies. The U.S.'s recent efforts to tighten AI chips exports and renewed tariffs have also weighed on investor sentiment.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index has fallen over 15% from its peak in May but picked up on Friday, likely supported by the signals of support from Beijing.

The Shanghai Composite Index was recently up 3.6%, the Shenzhen Composite Index was 6.8% higher and the tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index surged 10.6%, on track for its biggest one-day percentage gain in over two years.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

To the best of the knowledge and belief of the DCC Energy Directors (who have taken all reasonable care to ensure that such is the case), the information contained in this announcement is in accordance with the facts and does not omit anything likely to affect the import of such information.

Rule 8 – Dealing Disclosure Requirements

Under Rule 8.3(b) of the Irish Takeover Rules, any person ‘interested’ (directly or indirectly) in 1% or more of any class of ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy must disclose all ‘dealings’ in such ‘relevant securities’ during the ‘offer period’. The disclosure of a ‘dealing’ in ‘relevant securities’ by a person to whom Rule 8.3(b) applies must be made by no later than 3:30 p.m. (London time) on the business day following the date of the relevant transaction. This requirement will continue until the ‘offer period’ ends. If two or more persons co-operate on the basis of any agreement either express or tacit, either oral or written, to acquire an ‘interest’ in ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy, they will be deemed to be a single person for the purpose of Rule 8.3 of the Irish Takeover Rules. A dealing disclosure must contain the details specified in Rule 8.6(b) of the Irish Takeover Rules, including details of the dealing concerned and of the person’s interests and short positions in any ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy.

All ‘dealings’ in ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy by Bidco, or by any party ‘acting in concert’ with Bidco, must also be disclosed by no later than 12:00 noon (London time) on the ‘business day’ following the date of the relevant transaction. If two or more persons co-operate on the basis of an agreement, either express or tacit, either oral or written, to acquire for one or more of them an interest in relevant securities, they will be deemed to be a single person for these purposes.

Disclosure tables, giving details of the companies in whose ‘relevant securities’ and ‘dealings’ should be disclosed, can be found on the Irish Takeover Panel’s website at www.irishtakeoverpanel.ie.

‘Interests’ in securities arise, in summary, when a person has long economic exposure, whether conditional or absolute, to changes in the price of securities. In particular, a person will be treated as having an ‘interest’ by virtue of the ownership or control of securities, or by virtue of any option in respect of, or derivative referenced to, securities.

data.title: Shearwater announces third quarter 2026 results
data.description:
Bergen, 27 November 2026 – Shearwater Geoservices AS (“Shearwater” or the “Company”) today published the third quarter 2026 results. Revenue in the quarter was USD 107.0 million compared to USD 146.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. EBITDA was USD 14.7 million, (USD 5.2 million) reflecting a continued slow marine contract acquisition market in line with expectations.

Key takeaways:

· Soft Q3 contract activity due to few awards through 1H 2026

· Continued strong multi-client revenue contribution of USD 36 million

· 59% fleet utilisation across 7.3 active vessels, including one OBN crew

· End-Q3 backlog up 3.5x from Q2 to USD 755 million driven by strategic client awards

· Materially improved 2027 visibility, with three vessels fully committed for the year and high H1 coverage

Irene Basili, CEO of Shearwater, comments on the third quarter results:

"The third quarter reflected a continued soft contract market as anticipated, with low fleet utilisation following few projects awarded through first half of the year. At the same time, we benefitted from the organic build-up of our multi-client business with another strong quarterly contribution. We also made material commercial progress with several contract awards and new industry-backed multi-client surveys. We ended the quarter with a record USD 755 million backlog and a strong foundation for increased activity in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

Although it is too early to conclude that a sustained market recovery is underway, our visibility into 2027 is substantially improved. We have three vessels fully committed throughout the year and strong coverage across the active fleet for the first half. Additionally, more than 50% of our backlog comprises multi-year programmes, extending our scheduling horizon. The two large India surveys and the three-year OBN award offshore South America are important contributors, with the latter demonstrating the commercial potential of SW Tasman/Pearl platform.

That said, I want to emphasise that the stronger backlog does not change our commitment to disciplined fleet deployment and cost control. We prioritise utilisation for our active fleet at improved margins and are not planning for any vessel reactivations.

Our multi-client business reached two milestones in the period. First, we have commenced the Amapá survey offshore Brazil with SLB, a major programme adjacent to the Morpho discovery. Secondly, we just completed our first stand-alone survey in the Norwegian Sea. Both projects deploy our state-of-the-art Isometrix technology.

Recent awards, improved forward coverage and ongoing customer discussions are encouraging, and reflect the need for reserve replacement, energy security and exploration. Our focus remains on efficient operational delivery, securing quality backlog and investing selectively in multi-client opportunities. We enter the coming year with materially improved visibility and a more favourable market backdrop, while maintaining discipline on capacity and investments."

Webcast and conference call

CEO Irene Waage Basili and CFO Andreas Hveding Aubert will today at 14:00 CET host a webcast and conference call followed by Q&A.

Shearwater is a global marine geoscience and technology business that specialises in collecting data offshore. The organisation uses state-of-the art seismic vessels and equipment to explore beneath the seabed and processes the data using market-leading proprietary software. data.title: REG - Coca-Cola HBC AG - Completion of CCBA acquisition
data.description:
RNS Number : 9779E Coca-Cola HBC AG 27 November 2026  

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE.

Coca-Cola HBC AG

Completion of CCBA acquisition

Zug, Switzerland, 27 November 2026. Coca-Cola HBC AG ("Coca-Cola HBC" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of the Acquisition1 of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa ("CCBA") ("Completion"). Further to its announcement on 16 November 2026, Coca-Cola HBC is also pleased to confirm that it has received merger control approval from the Fair Competition Commission of Tanzania.

The Acquisition brings together two leading Coca-Cola bottlers, and Coca-Cola HBC is now the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler globally by volume[2], serving approximately 1.2 billion consumers and employing nearly 50,000 people.

Building on Coca-Cola HBC’s origins in Nigeria 75 years ago and its expansion into Egypt in 2022, the Acquisition materially expands Coca-Cola HBC’s presence in Africa, adding 14 markets and creating a stronger platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Coca-Cola HBC will now represent approximately two-thirds of Africa's Coca-Cola system volume and serve more than half of the continent's population, strengthening Coca-Cola HBC's position in a highly attractive growth region.

The transaction combines Coca-Cola HBC’s scale, resources and capabilities with CCBA’s strong market positions and deep local knowledge. It supports Coca-Cola HBC’s ambition to be the leading 24/7 beverage partner and it reinforces its long-standing strategic partnership with The Coca-Cola Company.

Anastassis G. David, Chairman of the Board of Coca-Cola HBC, commented:

“Today marks an important new chapter for us in Africa. As we welcome CCBA into the Coca-Cola HBC family, we do so with great respect for the legacy that has been built over generations and with a commitment to strengthening it for the future.

“On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank all the teams involved for their support in bringing this transaction to completion.”

Zoran Bogdanovic, Chief Executive Officer of Coca-Cola HBC, commented:

“The completion of the CCBA acquisition marks a historic milestone for Coca-Cola HBC. Africa is where our business began 75 years ago, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our presence across this incredible continent, creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Our listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange this week further underlines our long-term commitment to South Africa and the broader African continent.

"CCBA is a high-quality business with strong market positions, deep local knowledge and talented people. We are very pleased to welcome our new colleagues to Coca-Cola HBC. Together, we will invest in our leading 24/7 portfolio, our bespoke capabilities and our passionate people to capture the significant opportunities ahead.

“Our integration planning has been underway for many months, and we are ready to begin the next chapter of our growth story together with confidence and ambition.

"I would like to thank The Coca-Cola Company and the Gutsche family for their trust and partnership, and our teams across CCBA, Coca-Cola HBC and the wider Coca-Cola system for their commitment in completing this transaction. We look forward to working together to drive joint success."

Henrique Braun, Chief Executive Officer of The Coca-Cola Company, commented:

“This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations.

“CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth.”

Structure and financial effects

Coca-Cola HBC has acquired a 75% shareholding in CCBA from The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) and Gutsche Family Investments Pty Ltd (GFI), for a combined purchase price of $2.6 billion (at the time of signing). Coca-Cola HBC and TCCC have entered into a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire, or TCCC to sell, the remaining 25% stake in CCBA held by TCCC within a six-year period, with the call option exercisable between three and five years following Completion.

In connection with the Acquisition, Coca-Cola HBC will today issue 21,027,676 new ordinary shares to GFI, representing 5.45% of Coca-Cola HBC's enlarged issued and outstanding share capital. Admission to trading of the new ordinary shares on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, the Main Board of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the Main Market of Euronext Athens is expected to occur on Monday, 30 November 2026 at 08:00 (GMT), 09:00 (SAST) and 10:15 (EET), respectively.

The cash consideration for the Acquisition has been funded through a combination of existing liquidity and bonds issued by Coca-Cola HBC in March 2026 to refinance the bridge facilities entered into at signing. Leverage is expected to remain within Coca-Cola HBC’s medium-term target range of 1.5-2.0x Net debt to EBITDA. Coca-Cola HBC reconfirms that the transaction is expected to be low-single digit EPS accretive from the first full financial year post Completion.

For the purposes of UKLR 7.3.3R, Coca-Cola HBC confirms that there has been no material change affecting any matter contained in the announcement of the Acquisition.

With a vision to be the leading 24/7 beverage partner, we offer drinks for all occasions around the clock. Following the completion of our acquisition of a majority stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa on 27 November 2026, we now work together with our customers to serve more than 1.2 billion consumers across 43 markets in Europe and Africa.

Our portfolio is one of the strongest, broadest and most flexible in the beverage industry, with consumer-leading brands across the sparkling, adult sparkling, juice, water, sport, energy, ready-to-drink tea, coffee, and premium spirits categories, with snacks as an additional offering. Our products include Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, Fanta, Sprite, Schweppes, Kinley, Costa Coffee, Caffè Vergnano, Valser, Romerquelle, Dasani and other water brands, FuzeTea, Powerade, Cappy, Monster Energy, Finlandia Vodka, The Macallan, Jack Daniel's and Plazma. We foster an open and inclusive work environment for approximately 50,000 employees and believe that a positive environmental impact is integral to our future growth. data.title: Indian firms utilising only 20%-30% of free trade agreement benefits, RBI governor says
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Indian businesses are using only about 20%-30% of the benefits available under free-trade agreements (FTAs) compared with their foreign counterparts, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said at an event in Mumbai on Friday.

  • The comments come days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi said ⁠Indian industry should take advantage of opportunities from the free-trade agreements India has signed, including those with the ​EU and the ​UK

  • "The government of India has now opened up a number of avenues. A number of FTAs have been signed. At the same time, however, it has been found that only about 20% to 30% of the utilization has been done by Indians vis-à-vis 60% to 70% by our partners in the trade agreements," Malhotra said at an event for small and medium businesses

  • There is a long way to go for Indian businesses to take advantage of the lower tariffs negotiated under the agreements, he said

  • Small and medium businesses should learn more about the FTAs to improve quality, delivery timelines, standards and certifications, Malhotra added

  • The micro, small and medium enterprises sector has an AI adoption rate of about 14%, behind peers such as China, Malhotra said

  • India has free-trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand. Its proposed free-trade agreement with the European Union is expected to accelerate market-access ​opportunities and ​investment ⁠flows between India and the ⁠27-member ​EU bloc

  • Separately, ‌India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that India and the US were close ​to wrapping up a long-anticipated trade deal

  • Modi told industry leaders last week that Indian businesses could not take their huge domestic market for granted and urged them to compete globally ‌in an era when resources were being weaponised
